cues.text: Good morning everyone. My name’s Janet Parker and I’m the human resources manager.
We’re very happy to welcome you to your new apprenticeship.
I hope that the next six months will be a positive and enjoyable experience for you.
Most of you have very little or no experience of working for a big organisation and the
first week or so may be quite challenging.
There will be a lot of new information to take in, but the important thing is to check
with someone if you’re not sure what to do.
During your first week you’ll spend time in different departments, so make an effort to
talk to as many people as possible about their work.
You’ll make some new friends and find out lots of useful information.
As well as having a supervisor, you’ll each be assigned a mentor.
They won’t do your work for you, but they’ll ask what goals you’ve achieved so far, help
you identify areas for improvement, and you can discuss your more long-term ambitions
with them.
Now I just want to run through a few company policies.
You’ll have internet access for work, but please don’t use it for personal use.
Flexible working may be possible after your probationary period, but that will depend on
your department and your personal circumstances.
We ask that you don’t book any holidays until after your six-month apprenticeship has
finished.
There may be opportunities to do overtime during busy periods, and although you’re not
required to do this, it can be a valuable experience.
We don’t have a formal dress code.
You may wear casual clothes as long as they’re practical, and comfortable shoes like
trainers are preferable.
There’s also a subsidised canteen on site, so we’ve decided to introduce a no packed
lunch policy.
